reads.title: ‘If you build something vastly smarter than you, it better be on your side’: can we stop AI from deceiving us?
reads.author: Snigdha Poonam
reads.note: A reported journey into the emerging science of machine deception—and the race to test whether increasingly capable AI systems are merely failing, strategically scheming, or learning to hide the difference.

reads.title: The Rise of the Science Sleuths
reads.author: Jessica Wapner
reads.note: Inside the loose international network finding manipulated images and fabricated data in published research—and the institutional resistance that turns a correction into a battle over how science polices itself.

reads.title: Fear and Fragility: The Glass Delusion and Its History
reads.author: Tamara Sanderson
reads.note: Why did people across early modern Europe become convinced that their bodies were made of glass? A history of a vanished delusion as a language for trauma, social pressure, transparency, and fear.

reads.title: Ladies of the ’80s
reads.author: Lisa Whittington-Hill
reads.note: A personal and cultural history of the women who remade 1980s popular music, expanded the era’s visual vocabulary, and showed generations of listeners how individuality could become a form of power.

reads.title: To Dismantle the Concept of Separate but Equal, Thurgood Marshall Methodically Devised a Winning Strategy: Divide and Conquer
reads.author: Victor Luckerson
reads.note: Brown v. Board did not arrive in a single leap. This account traces the students, cases, and deliberately accumulated precedents through which Thurgood Marshall made an entrenched legal doctrine collapse.
